Consider a directed weighted graph G(V, E), where V is the set of vertices and E is the set of edges. Suppose we use adjacency list to implement the graph. Consider a sequence of |V| operations with each corresponding to a different vertex in V. For the operation for vertex v, the cost is assumed to be the number of outgoing edges from v.  (a) What is the cost of the worst possible single operation in this sequence of operations? (b) What is the average amortized cost of the above sequence of operations based on aggregate analysis?

message.content:
In an adjacency list representation, the cost of a single operation for a vertex v is equal to its out-degree. The worst-case scenario occurs when one specific vertex has all possible outgoing edges connected to it. Therefore, the maximum cost of any single operation in this sequence is $|V| - 1$.

To determine the amortized cost using aggregate analysis, we sum the costs of all operations and divide by the total number of operations. The sum of all out-degrees in the graph is equal to the total number of edges $|E|$, so the average amortized cost per operation is $\frac{|E|}{|V|}$.

*   The worst-case single operation cost is bounded by the maximum out-degree, which can be at most $|V|-1$ in a complete directed graph without self-loops.
*   The aggregate analysis shows that the total work done over all $|V|$ operations is exactly $|E|$, leading to an amortized cost of $\frac{|E|}{|V|}$ per operation.
